sources.entry: Eleven - Open-source reverse-engineering app where coding agents read, rename and patch binaries, Android apps and GPU kernels alongside you. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Zfinix/eleven) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Eleven is an open-source, agent-first reverse-engineering app for macOS, Windows and Linux where coding agents read, rename and suggest patches for binaries, Android apps, and GPU kernels alongside you.
summary.what_it_does: Eleven opens native binaries (Mach-O, ELF, PE) through Ghidra via REA or through Rizin for faster loading, showing functions, pseudocode, assembly, a control-flow graph, cross-references, strings, segments and hex. Android APKs open with Java from jadx, smali from apktool when installed, and resources, manifest and native libraries listed alongside. Users select code and ask an ACP-compatible agent to explain it, rename functions, add notes or propose byte patches, with changes logged and undoable. Agents can also drive the UI through Eleven's own MCP tools. The app also covers GPU kernels (CUDA and HIP fat binaries as PTX), Metal shaders and ML model files, and can rewrite pseudocode in several languages. Other features include projects saved as .eleven files, patching copies of binaries, diffing two builds, running programs under LLDB, and exporting pseudocode, assembly, or CFGs as PDF.
use_cases: reverse engineer a macOS app or binary
have an AI agent rename functions in decompiled code
compare two builds of a program
inspect CUDA or Metal GPU kernels
patch bytes in a binary and save a copy
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash  (macOS 14+ Apple Silicon installer; installs Eleven.app)
Linux x64: download the AppImage or .tar.gz from the latest release
git clone the repo, then cd eleven/app
notable: Agent-first design: any ACP-compatible agent can open functions, rename, add notes and propose patches while the user approves changes in the same window
Two analysis engines: Ghidra (slower, clearest pseudocode) and Rizin (opens most apps in seconds)
Covers GPU kernels (CUDA/HIP PTX, rewrites to CUDA C++, HIP C++ or Metal), Metal shaders and ML model formats
Projects saved as shareable single .eleven files; original binaries are never modified
caveats: Install scripts target specific platforms: macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, Windows x64, Linux x64
Building from source requires Bun, Node 20+, Ghidra, a JDK, and a checkout of REA 6.x next to the repo
Ghidra path requires Ghidra 12.x with Java 21; Android analysis needs jadx installed separately
The README says Eleven is free and built by one person, with sponsorship funding signed releases and the debugger
